title: Guidelines and Conditions for Arts Funding
what_it_is: Guidelines and Conditions for Arts Funding

sections.label: NAC funding guidelines
sections.summary: The National Arts Council requires applicants to meet its publicly available funding guidelines, updated in 2013 and still relevant.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: As a steward of public funds, the National Arts Council (NAC) seeks to enlarge the space for the arts to flourish without compromising on social cohesion and stability.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: Hence, applicants will need to meet NAC's funding guidelines, which are public available on its website.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: They were updated recently in 2013 and are still relevant.

sections.label: Major Grant scheme review
sections.summary: In 2016, NAC conducted a year-long review of the Major Grant scheme involving over 100 arts community members.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: For example, in 2016, NAC conducted an extensive year-long review of the Major Grant scheme, involving more than 100 members from the arts community.

sections.label: Declined or withdrawn funding cases
sections.summary: Few projects were declined or withdrawn funding, with no such cases this year except Sonny Liew's and Jeremy Tiang's works.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: The number of projects that were declined funding or withdrawn funding based on this ruling are very, very few.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Currently, I do not have the exact details at hand, but I would say, this year, except for those in the public domain, Sonny Liew's Art of Charlie Chan as well as Jeremy Tiang's novel, there are no such cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: As a disburser of public funds, the Government does not allow the funds to be used to advance the agenda of any political party.

sections.label: Political party accountability for past decisions
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether this falls under the prohibition and says any political party remains accountable for past decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Would this come under the prohibition that the Parliamentary Secretary has mentioned?

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: I think for any political party, the party would be still accountable and responsible for decisions made in the past.
